slides.headline: War, Ceasefires, and the Verification Gap
slides.subheadline: The supplied article traces regional escalation; its claims are not independently verified.
slides.svgBlueprint: Use Paper #101923, Ink #EEF0EB, Accent #D9B45B, and Surface #1C2A36 throughout. Draw a central horizontal line interrupted by jagged breaks, symbolizing interrupted diplomacy rather than measured intensity. Place two annotations on opposite edges. Reserve the upper third for the headline; keep all SVG labels outside text zones.

items.label: 28 February 2026
items.body: Reported start of US–Israeli strikes and war with Iran and regional allies.

items.label: Opening strikes
items.body: Hundreds of air strikes across Iran; no exact count supplied.

slides.headline: Escalation Preceded the Opening Strikes
slides.subheadline: The article connects the Gaza war, earlier attacks, and a US military buildup.
slides.svgBlueprint: Draw three ascending Surface platforms joined by an Accent hairline. Place dates above platforms and bodies below. Use equal platform dimensions; elevation indicates narrative sequence, not measured escalation. No proportional time axis.

items.body: The Gaza war triggered the wider Middle Eastern crisis, the article says.

items.label: June 2025
items.body: Israel attacked military and nuclear facilities; US strikes also targeted nuclear facilities.

items.label: January–February 2026
items.body: US regional military buildup described as largest since the 2003 invasion of Iraq.

slides.headline: A Threat Claim Meets Another Timeline
slides.subheadline: The article juxtaposes Trump's missile claim with a reported US intelligence assessment.
slides.svgBlueprint: Create exactly two contrasting text columns, framed by opposing open brackets. Use an Accent divider without arrows or magnitude bars. Anchor each date above its respective text; do not imply the statements describe identical development stages.

items.label: February 2026
items.body: Trump said Iran was developing missiles capable of striking the United States.
Reported US intelligence assessment: Iran needed until 2035 to build US-threatening missiles.

slides.headline: Unverified Does Not Mean Weaponizing
slides.subheadline: The article reports separate IAEA findings in February 2026—not equivalent assurances.
slides.svgBlueprint: Draw an incomplete circular inspection boundary at center. Connect two equal-sized callouts with neutral leader lines. Use a gap rather than a warning symbol to communicate incomplete verification. Avoid progress percentages, weapon icons, or any implication of confirmed weaponization.

items.label: Verification limits
items.body: The IAEA could not verify enrichment suspension or confirm the stockpile's status.

items.label: Weaponization finding
items.body: The IAEA found no evidence Iran was weaponizing, according to the article.

slides.headline: Inspection Access Split Along Strike Lines
slides.subheadline: The article distinguishes bombed nuclear facilities from unaffected facilities.
slides.svgBlueprint: Draw one neutral inspection entry line branching toward exactly two schematic facility outlines. End the bombed-facilities branch at a closed gate; continue the unaffected-facilities branch through an open gate. Buildings are generic symbols, not locations or facility counts.

items.label: Bombed facilities
items.body: Iran denied the IAEA access to bombed nuclear facilities.

items.label: Unaffected facilities
items.body: Iran provided the IAEA access to unaffected facilities.

slides.headline: A Ceasefire Under Immediate Strain
slides.subheadline: The article traces a truce, failed talks, and a blockade.
slides.svgBlueprint: Place three evenly spaced event nodes along a horizontal Accent rail. Interrupt the rail beneath the talks node with a narrow gap. Give each node one date and one compact body. Equal spacing is schematic, not elapsed time.

items.label: 8 April
items.body: A two-week ceasefire began; Israel launched massive airstrikes across Lebanon.

items.label: 12–13 April
items.body: Islamabad Talks failed; the United States subsequently imposed a naval blockade on Iran.

items.label: 21 April
items.body: The United States announced an indefinite ceasefire.

slides.headline: Agreements Did Not Hold
slides.subheadline: The article reports a memorandum, renewed ceasefire, and another collapse.
slides.svgBlueprint: Create a narrow ribbon descending through three alternating bends, with one event at each bend. Finish with an open break beside the final event. Use identical event markers; ribbon direction represents sequence, not a quantitative diplomatic score.

items.label: 17 June
items.body: The United States and Iran signed a memorandum and lifted the dual blockade.

items.label: 28 June
items.body: The United States and Iran agreed to resume the ceasefire after brief escalation.

items.label: 8 July
items.body: Article attributes ceasefire collapse to Iranian attacks on commercial vessels in Hormuz.

slides.headline: Disruption Spread Beyond the Battlefield
slides.subheadline: The article calls oil disruption the largest ever, without volumes or comparative data.
slides.svgBlueprint: Stack three full-width Surface bands separated by generous Paper gutters. Add a small abstract symbol at each band's left edge: interrupted flow, oscillating line, and household outline. Keep bands equal-sized; do not encode unsupplied economic magnitudes or causal relationships.

items.label: Disrupted sectors
items.body: Natural gas, fertilizer, aviation, tourism, and shipping faced disruption.

items.label: Financial pressures
items.body: Financial-market volatility, inflation, lower economic growth, and higher borrowing costs.

items.label: Household consequences
items.body: Higher fuel and energy prices; global cost-of-living crisis; protests in Europe and elsewhere.

slides.headline: The Toll Is Only Partly Quantified
slides.subheadline: The spending estimate carries an [update] marker; it is not a comprehensive global cost.
slides.svgBlueprint: Build an open ledger with a large upper spending entry and a smaller lower casualty entry separated by a thin rule. Render complete amounts and qualifiers as text, not standalone telemetry badges. Do not use bars, casualty pictograms, or proportional areas.

items.label: US Department of Defense estimate
items.body: $47.1 billion in US military spending as of October 2026.

items.label: Civilian and military casualties
items.body: Thousands; no exact total, national breakdown, or separation of deaths and injuries.

slides.headline: An Article Is Not Independent Verification
slides.subheadline: The dossier records reported claims; its underlying cited documents were not supplied.
slides.svgBlueprint: Place a large outlined document silhouette on the left, ending in a visibly interrupted bottom edge. Put exactly two margin notes on the right, connected to citation placeholders and the interrupted edge. Use generic marks rather than invented reference numbers or source logos.

items.label: Missing source documents
items.body: Bracketed references appear, but their underlying source documents are not included.

items.label: Incomplete excerpt
items.body: The supplied excerpt ends mid-citation after its final reference to Operation Roaring Lion.
